assertions.name: crossing_energy_orientation_matches_the_published_pair
assertions.source: electron 3.32993574825 vs ~3.330, positron -2.70275485187 vs ~-2.703 (pair-creation-energy.md). A reversed sign convention would swap these, so the orientation is pinned before any verdict is read off the functional

assertions.name: a_gamma_gamma_vertex_contributes_exactly_h
assertions.source: sigma_i sigma_{i+1}^-1 = q + (-1/q) = h = 0.20906029879563931543, reproducing part 7's closed form independently

assertions.name: E_cross_on_gg_words_is_k_times_h_so_energy_IS_count_there
assertions.source: a 5-vertex gg word has E_cross = 1.0453014939781965772 = 5h exactly. On gg words energy is PROPORTIONAL to count, so part 7 is right that swapping the cost changes nothing there -- and E_cross(empty) = 0 is below every non-empty gg word, which is its degeneracy

assertions.name: count_and_energy_select_DIFFERENT_gluons
assertions.source: crossing count TIES ['sigma_1', 'sigma_1^-1'] at k = 1; crossing energy strictly prefers sigma_1^-1 at -0.900918283956. The two costs do not agree on this family, so the choice of cost is a real decision rather than a formality -- the owner's objection, measured

assertions.name: sigma_1_inv_strictly_beats_sigma_1_by_energy_while_tying_by_count
assertions.source: sigma_1^-1 E = -0.900918283956 < sigma_1 E = 1.10997858275, both at k = 1 and both reading-3-feasible. A negative crossing carries NEGATIVE energy, which no count can see

assertions.name: the_empty_word_is_NOT_the_energy_minimum_on_the_gluon_family
assertions.source: -0.900918283956 < 0.0. gg words are sign-BALANCED by construction so every non-empty one costs a positive multiple of h; the gluon is outside that construction and admits a bare negative crossing. So the degeneracy that retired this functional in part 7 is specific to gg words and does NOT transfer -- crossing energy is usable here

assertions.name: crossing_energy_is_order_blind_and_ties_the_two_crossing_gluons
assertions.source: E_cross is a sum over letters, so reordering is invisible (0.0 apart) and all 3 feasible 2-crossing gluons tie at one value. It breaks the k = 1 tie and leaves the k = 2 tie standing -- which is why an EMBEDDING energy, not a letter-sum, is what the question actually needs

description: Crossing COUNT is the cost FrobeniusSelected is instantiated with; the owner objected that it is a combinatorial proxy and a stabiliser that adds a crossing may lower the energy. Measured: on gamma-gamma words part 7's verdict holds exactly (E_cross = k*h, so energy is proportional to count and the empty word is the minimum), but the gluon dressing is NOT a gg word and there the two costs DISAGREE -- sigma_1 and sigma_1^-1 tie at count 1 while sigma_1^-1 = -0.9009 strictly beats sigma_1 = +1.1100 by energy. The degeneracy also dissolves: E_cross(empty) = 0 is NOT minimal once negative crossings are available, which gg words never have. But E_cross is a letter-sum and stays order-blind -- the three two-crossing feasible gluons tie exactly -- so it breaks one tie and not the other. Points at an embedding energy (O'Hara/Moebius via Bring), for which the corpus has the integrator but NO braid-word-to-curve map.

open_target_not_attempted.missing: any map from a braid word to a curve in or on the Bring surface; the integrators consume hand-parametrised named embeddings (Hopf, Borromean). Searched computations/ and tools/ -- an absence on those surfaces, not a proof of absence
open_target_not_attempted.hard_part: Moebius energy is a property of an EMBEDDING and is not a knot invariant (the invariant is the infimum over the isotopy class), so a bridge needs the minimiser or a canonical embedding -- which is what the Bring surface would be for
